title: Faire and aller
goal: Say what you do and where you go with the irregular verbs faire and aller, using au, à la, à l' and aux.

items.fr: je fais, nous faisons, vous faites, ils font
items.en: faire (to do, to make) in the present

drills.en: We do the shopping on Saturdays.

drills.explain: ils → font, like ils sont, ils ont, ils vont.

items.fr: je vais, tu vas, il va, nous allons, vous allez, ils vont

drills.en: I go to work at 8 o'clock.
Are you going to the bank?

drills.prompt: “They go to school.” Which is correct?
drills.explain: aller is irregular: ils vont. Before a vowel, la/le become l': à l'école.

items.fr: au, à la, à l', aux
items.en: à + le = au, à + les = aux

drills.explain: le travail → à + le = au travail.
les cours → à + les = aux cours.
la banque → à la banque: à + la does not change.

example.en: In the evening, I do the cooking.

example.en: We do the shopping on Saturdays.

example.en: He does the housework on Sundays.

Are you going to the bank?

example.fr: Qu'est-ce que tu fais le samedi ?
example.en: What do you do on Saturdays?

steps.title: What do you do on Saturdays?

blocks.title: Friday afternoon at the office in Vancouver
blocks.context: Olivier and Camille are colleagues. They talk about their Saturdays.

lines.speaker: Olivier
lines.fr: Camille, qu'est-ce que tu fais le samedi ?
lines.en: Camille, what do you do on Saturdays?

lines.speaker: Camille
lines.fr: Le matin, je fais du sport et je vais à la banque. Et toi ?
lines.en: In the morning, I exercise and I go to the bank. And you?

lines.speaker: Olivier
lines.fr: Moi, je fais les courses le matin et je fais le ménage l'après-midi.
lines.en: Me, I do the shopping in the morning and I do the housework in the afternoon.

lines.speaker: Camille
lines.fr: L'après-midi, mon mari et moi, nous allons aux cours de français.
lines.en: In the afternoon, my husband and I go to French classes.

lines.speaker: Olivier
lines.fr: Le samedi ? Vous allez à l'école le samedi !
lines.en: On Saturdays? You go to school on Saturdays!

lines.speaker: Camille
lines.fr: Eh oui ! Et le soir, on fait la cuisine pour les enfants.
lines.en: Yes indeed! And in the evening, we do the cooking for the kids.

lines.speaker: Olivier
lines.fr: Et les enfants, qu'est-ce qu'ils font ?
lines.en: And the kids, what do they do?

lines.speaker: Camille
lines.fr: Ils font du sport le samedi. Le lundi, ils vont à l'école et moi, je vais au travail.
lines.en: They do sports on Saturdays. On Mondays, they go to school and I go to work.

lines.speaker: Olivier
lines.fr: Bravo ! Moi, le samedi soir, je vais au cinéma.
lines.en: Well done! Me, on Saturday evenings, I go to the movies.

blocks.body: Two very common verbs appear again and again: [[faire]] (*fais, font*) and [[aller]] (*vais, allons, vont*). Spot them before you look at the English.

blocks.title: Faire: to do, to make
blocks.body: [[Faire]] is irregular, like [[être]] and [[avoir]]. It means *to do* or *to make*, and French uses it for many everyday activities where English uses other verbs: *cook*, *shop*, *clean*, *exercise*.

blocks.title: Faire in the present
head: faire
English
blocks.note: [[fais]], [[fais]], [[fait]] all sound like *fay*. [[Faisons]] is said *fe-zon*, as if it were spelled *fesons*. [[Vous faites]] is irregular: never *faisez*.

blocks.title: Everyday chores with faire
blocks.pattern: faire + la cuisine / les courses / le ménage / du sport
blocks.note: Learn these as fixed chunks. The [[du]] in [[faire du sport]] is explained in Unit 6; for now, just copy it.

examples.fr: Nous faisons les courses le samedi.
examples.en: We do the shopping on Saturdays.

blocks.title: Aller (to go) in the present
head: aller
English
blocks.note: [[Aller]] ends in -er but it is **irregular**. Only [[nous allons]] and [[vous allez]] look like a normal -er verb. Link: [[nous‿allons]], [[vous‿allez]].

blocks.title: Going somewhere: à + the article
head: the place
à + article
example
rows: Je vais aux cours de français.
blocks.note: [[à + le]] always becomes [[au]] and [[à + les]] always becomes [[aux]]. [[À la]] and [[à l']] don't change. You already met [[au]] in [[au Canada]]. With a city, there is no article: [[Je vais à Toronto]].

blocks.title: Four look-alikes
blocks.body:
Four very common verbs end in **-ont** with ils/elles. Learn them together:

- [[ils sont]] (être): *eel son*
- [[ils‿ont]] (avoir): *eel zon*, with a z liaison
- [[ils font]] (faire): *eel fon*
- [[ils vont]] (aller): *eel von*

The only difference is the first sound: **s**, **z**, **f**, **v**. Listen carefully!

examples.en: They are going to the bank.

blocks.body:
- **à le, à les:** [[Je vais à le travail]] ✗ → [[Je vais au travail]]. [[à les cours]] ✗ → [[aux cours]].
- **vous faisez:** ✗ → [[vous faites]].
- **ils allent:** ✗ → [[ils vont]].
- **Forgetting the article:** [[Je vais à banque]] ✗ → [[Je vais à la banque]]. With a city, no article: [[à Toronto]].
- **Going home:** for *I'm going home*, use [[je rentre]] (Lesson 1). It is the most natural way to say it.

blocks.title: Faire l'épicerie
blocks.body:
In Québec, people usually say [[faire l'épicerie]] for grocery shopping. [[L'épicerie]] is the grocery store, and also the groceries themselves. In France you will hear [[faire les courses]]. Both are understood everywhere.

Two more Québec words: [[magasiner]] (to go shopping for clothes and other things, an -er verb) and [[le dépanneur]] (the corner store). And many people in Québec bank at a [[caisse]] (a credit union), so you will hear [[Je vais à la caisse]].

examples.fr: Je fais l'épicerie le jeudi soir.
examples.en: I do my grocery shopping on Thursday evenings. (Québec)

blocks.title: Listen and repeat
blocks.note: Repeat each line. Watch the first sound of sont / ont / font / vont.

lines.tip: vont: a v sound and a nasal vowel, no t.

lines.fr: Elles vont aux cours de français.

blocks.explain: [[faire le ménage]] = to do the housework. [[Font]] starts with an f sound: it is faire.

options: They are going to the bank.
blocks.explain: [[vont]] starts with a v: aller. [[Ils sont]] (s) would mean *they are*; [[ils‿ont]] (z) would mean *they have*.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.intro: Answer without scrolling back. Remember: au and aux are just à + le and à + les.

blocks.en: What do you do on Sundays?
blocks.explain: vous → faites, one of only three verbs with a vous form not in -ez (êtes, faites, dites).

blocks.en: I go to work at 8 o'clock.

blocks.text: Elles vont ___ cours de français le soir.
blocks.en: They go to French classes in the evening.

blocks.prompt: “They go to work.” Which is correct?
optionFeedback: font is faire (to do), not aller.
Ils sont au travail means they ARE at work.

blocks.prompt: I do the housework on Saturdays.
accept: Je fais le ménage le samedi.
Le samedi, je fais le ménage.
Le samedi je fais le ménage.
Je fais le ménage tous les samedis.
blocks.explain: faire le ménage = do the housework; le samedi = every Saturday.

blocks.prompt: Are you going to the bank? (to a friend)
accept: Est-ce que tu vas à la banque ?
blocks.explain: tu → vas; la banque → à la banque.

blocks.prompt: We often go to French classes.
accept: Nous allons souvent aux cours de français.
Souvent nous allons aux cours de français.
blocks.explain: souvent goes after the verb; à + les cours = aux cours.

blocks.prompt: Match each chunk to its meaning.

blocks.fr: Elles font la cuisine le soir.
blocks.explain: [[font]]: f sound, so it is faire. Listen to the subject: [[elles]] (with an l sound) is not [[ils]].

blocks.prompt: On Sundays, I get up late and I go to the movies.
accept: Le dimanche, je me lève tard et je vais au cinéma.
Le dimanche je me lève tard et je vais au cinéma.
Je me lève tard le dimanche et je vais au cinéma.
blocks.explain: Reflexive [[je me lève]] + [[je vais au cinéma]] (à + le = au).

blocks.prompt: A colleague asks: Qu'est-ce que tu fais le samedi ? Answer with at least two things you do and two places you go.
checklist: Two chunks with faire (les courses, le ménage, la cuisine, du sport)
Two places with aller (au, à la, à l', aux)

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Le samedi matin, je fais les courses et je vais à la banque. L'après-midi, je fais le ménage. Le soir, je vais au cinéma avec ma sœur. Et toi, qu'est-ce que tu fais le samedi ?
models.en: On Saturday mornings, I do the shopping and I go to the bank. In the afternoon, I do the housework. In the evening, I go to the movies with my sister. And you, what do you do on Saturdays?

blocks.prompt: Write a short text about who does what in your home and where everyone goes during the week.
checklist: Use faire with at least two different persons (je fais, il fait, nous faisons…)
Use aller with at least two different persons
Use au and one of à la / à l' / aux
Add one frequency word (souvent, toujours, le samedi…)

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: À la maison, je fais la cuisine et mon mari fait le ménage. Le samedi, nous faisons les courses ensemble. Le lundi, je vais au travail à 8 heures et les enfants vont à l'école. Le mardi soir, nous allons aux cours de français.
models.en: At home, I do the cooking and my husband does the housework. On Saturdays, we do the shopping together. On Mondays, I go to work at 8 and the children go to school. On Tuesday evenings, we go to French classes.

summary:
- Conjugate **faire** ([[je fais… nous faisons, vous faites, ils font]]) and **aller** ([[je vais… nous allons, vous allez, ils vont]])
- Talk about chores: [[faire la cuisine, les courses, le ménage, du sport]]
- Say where you go: [[au travail, à la banque, à l'école, aux cours]] (à + le = au, à + les = aux)
